label: good
seen: No measurement of this game exists; none was taken, and I saw no score of it or of any parent. Its moves and results were compared with Fairy-Stockfish's translation of it (chess-variant-sandbox fairy, pyffish 0.0.90), whose opening is the built-in clobber's, never played by this project's players.

evidence.says: devised in 2001 by Michael H. Albert, J. P. Grossman and Richard Nowakowski; a Computer Olympiad event since 2005; a report on the Clobber competition at Tilburg in 2011; the rules: a full checkerboard of stones, a move takes an orthogonally adjacent enemy stone, the player who cannot move loses; the starting position shown on 5x6

tier_note: W: recorded tournaments, but mostly between programs (the Computer Olympiad), so flagged thin record as unlike-search.md section 1.2 row 3 says. L: 2001 to today, 20 to 50 years.
departure: none in the rules (the first player, which the source leaves open, is the one with a stone on b1, Fairy-Stockfish's); flagged thin record: its organised play is mostly between programs
addition: unlike-search.md R-S10b1: a published game of section 1.2, row 3; not in the labelled set's registered reading (labelled-set.md section 3.3)
